questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: The first-line drug treatment for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in a school-age child is:
questions.concept: Stimulants increase synaptic dopamine and noradrenaline in prefrontal circuits and are highly effective. Growth and appetite are monitored; atomoxetine is a non-stimulant alternative where misuse or tics are a concern.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: Electroconvulsive therapy is most strongly indicated in:
options: Severe depression with stupor, refusal to eat or high suicidal risk
questions.concept: ECT acts faster than any antidepressant, making it the treatment of choice when delay is dangerous, and is also used in catatonia, puerperal psychosis and neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Memory disturbance is the main adverse effect.
questions.reference: Kaplan & Sadock Synopsis 12e, Brain Stimulation Therapies

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: The only absolute contraindication to electroconvulsive therapy is:
questions.concept: Raised intracranial pressure risks herniation. Pregnancy, old age and cardiac devices are relative considerations, and ECT is in fact often preferred in pregnancy to avoid teratogenic drugs.
questions.reference: Kaplan & Sadock Synopsis 12e, Brain Stimulation Therapies

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: Lithium requires regular monitoring because:
options: It has a narrow therapeutic index with renal and thyroid toxicity
questions.concept: Serum levels are kept at 0.6 to 1.0 mmol/L; toxicity causes coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, confusion and seizures. Thiazides, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors and dehydration raise levels dangerously.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: Clozapine is reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and requires monitoring for:
options: Agranulocytosis by regular white cell counts
questions.concept: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic in resistant illness and reduces suicidality, but causes agranulocytosis in about 1%, plus myocarditis, seizures, weight gain and hypersalivation, mandating registry-based blood monitoring.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is characterised by:
options: Hyperthermia, lead-pipe rigidity, autonomic instability and raised creatine kinase
questions.concept: NMS follows dopamine blockade, developing over days, and is treated by stopping the antipsychotic with cooling, dantrolene and bromocriptine. Serotonin syndrome differs in having hyperreflexia, clonus and diarrhoea with rapid onset.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: Tardive dyskinesia is:
options: A late-onset involuntary orofacial movement disorder from prolonged dopamine blockade
questions.concept: Tardive dyskinesia emerges after months to years of antipsychotic use and may be irreversible, so the lowest effective dose is used. Acute dystonia occurring within days responds promptly to anticholinergics.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: Cognitive behaviour therapy works on the principle that:
options: Maladaptive thoughts drive emotions and behaviour, and can be identified and modified
questions.concept: CBT is structured, time-limited and problem-focused with homework, and has the strongest evidence base in depression, anxiety disorders and OCD. Psychoanalysis instead explores unconscious conflict over a long period.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: Systematic desensitisation for phobia involves:
options: Graded exposure to a hierarchy of feared stimuli paired with relaxation
questions.concept: Reciprocal inhibition pairs relaxation with progressively more anxiety-provoking stimuli. Flooding instead uses immediate maximal exposure, and both work by preventing avoidance so anxiety extinguishes naturally.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.stem: Enuresis in a child older than 5 years is best managed initially with:
options: Behavioural measures including an enuresis alarm and motivational therapy
questions.concept: Alarms have the best long-term cure rates with no drug exposure. Desmopressin is useful for short-term cover such as school trips, and imipramine is now rarely used because of cardiotoxicity in overdose.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: A sunburst periosteal reaction with Codman triangle in the metaphysis of a long bone suggests:
questions.concept: Aggressive periosteal elevation produces the Codman triangle, and spiculated new bone perpendicular to the cortex gives the sunburst appearance, typical of osteosarcoma around the knee in adolescents.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: An onion-peel (lamellated) periosteal reaction in the diaphysis of a long bone in a child suggests:
questions.concept: Successive layers of periosteal new bone give the onion-skin pattern, characteristic of Ewing sarcoma, which is diaphyseal and may mimic osteomyelitis with fever and raised inflammatory markers.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: A soap-bubble appearance in the epiphysis of the distal femur in a young adult indicates:
questions.concept: Giant cell tumour is an eccentric expansile lytic epiphyseal lesion with a narrow zone of transition abutting subchondral bone, giving a multiloculated soap-bubble look. It is locally aggressive with high recurrence.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: Multiple punched-out lytic skull lesions without marginal sclerosis are characteristic of:
questions.concept: Myeloma is purely lytic with no osteoblastic reaction, so lesions have no sclerotic rim and bone scans are typically negative - hence skeletal survey rather than scintigraphy is used for staging.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: A sequestrum on radiograph in chronic osteomyelitis represents:
options: Dead avascular bone within an involucrum of new bone
questions.concept: The sequestrum is dense necrotic bone acting as a nidus for persistent infection, surrounded by the involucrum of reactive new bone with cloacae draining pus. Surgical removal is required for cure.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: Looser zones (pseudofractures) are characteristic of:
questions.concept: Looser zones are transverse translucent bands with sclerotic margins at sites of stress - pubic rami, femoral neck, ribs and scapula - reflecting unmineralised osteoid, and are pathognomonic of osteomalacia.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: Bamboo spine on a lumbar radiograph indicates:
options: Ankylosing spondylitis with syndesmophytes and ligamentous ossification
questions.concept: Vertical syndesmophytes bridging vertebral bodies with ossification of spinal ligaments fuse the spine into a rigid bamboo-like column, preceded by bilateral symmetrical sacroiliitis which is the earliest sign.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: A rat-bite or pencil-in-cup deformity of the digits suggests:
questions.concept: Psoriatic arthritis causes both erosion and proliferation, producing pencil-in-cup deformity and arthritis mutilans with distal interphalangeal involvement, unlike rheumatoid arthritis which spares the DIP joints.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: A hair-on-end appearance of the skull vault is characteristic of:
options: Thalassaemia major and other chronic haemolytic anaemias
questions.concept: Marrow hyperplasia widens the diploic space and thins the outer table, with vertical trabeculae producing the hair-on-end pattern, along with maxillary overgrowth giving chipmunk facies.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.stem: Subperiosteal bone resorption of the radial aspect of the middle phalanges is pathognomonic of:
questions.concept: Subperiosteal resorption, best seen on the radial border of the middle phalanges of the index and middle fingers, is the most specific radiological sign of hyperparathyroidism, with salt-and-pepper skull and brown tumours.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: The initial investigation of choice in suspected acute stroke is:
options: Non-contrast CT of the head to exclude haemorrhage
questions.concept: Non-contrast CT rapidly distinguishes haemorrhagic from ischaemic stroke, which determines whether thrombolysis can be given. Early ischaemic changes may be subtle, while blood appears immediately hyperdense.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: A biconvex (lentiform) hyperdense collection that does not cross suture lines indicates:
questions.concept: Extradural blood is limited by firm dural attachment at sutures, producing a lens shape, whereas subdural blood spreads freely across sutures in a crescent but is limited by dural reflections at the midline.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: Blood in the basal cisterns on non-contrast CT indicates:
questions.concept: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage fills the basal cisterns and sylvian fissures. If CT is negative but suspicion is high, lumbar puncture at 12 hours for xanthochromia is required, followed by CT angiography.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: MRI is superior to CT for imaging:
options: Posterior fossa, brainstem and early ischaemia by diffusion-weighted imaging
questions.concept: MRI avoids beam-hardening artefact in the posterior fossa and detects cytotoxic oedema within minutes on diffusion-weighted sequences. CT remains superior for acute blood, bone and calcification, and is faster.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: Multiple ring-enhancing lesions in an HIV-positive patient most likely represent:
questions.concept: Toxoplasmosis typically gives multiple lesions in the basal ganglia and at the grey-white junction. Primary CNS lymphoma is usually solitary and periventricular; failure to respond to empirical anti-toxoplasma therapy prompts biopsy.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: A butterfly lesion crossing the corpus callosum with irregular ring enhancement suggests:
questions.concept: Glioblastoma spreads across the corpus callosum giving the butterfly pattern, with central necrosis, irregular enhancement and marked vasogenic oedema. It is the commonest primary malignant brain tumour in adults.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: An extra-axial dural-based mass with homogeneous enhancement and a dural tail is characteristic of:
questions.concept: Meningiomas arise from arachnoid cap cells, are extra-axial with a broad dural base, enhance avidly and homogeneously, may calcify and cause hyperostosis of adjacent bone.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: Restricted diffusion on DWI with low ADC within a ring-enhancing lesion favours:
options: Pyogenic brain abscess over necrotic tumour
questions.concept: Viscous pus restricts water diffusion, whereas necrotic tumour does not, making DWI the key discriminator between abscess and cystic or necrotic neoplasm when enhancement patterns overlap.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: Periventricular calcification in a neonate suggests congenital infection with:
questions.concept: CMV causes periventricular calcification with microcephaly, while toxoplasmosis causes scattered diffuse intracranial calcification with hydrocephalus and chorioretinitis - a useful distinguishing pattern.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: CNS imaging: CT/MRI in stroke, trauma & space-occupying lesions
questions.stem: The hyperdense middle cerebral artery sign on non-contrast CT indicates:
options: Acute thrombus within the vessel, an early sign of infarction
questions.concept: A hyperdense artery represents fresh intraluminal thrombus and is one of the earliest CT signs of ischaemic stroke, appearing before parenchymal changes such as loss of grey-white differentiation and insular ribbon sign.
